--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.cmty_label_propagation()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Detect communities by asynchronous label propagation. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.cmty_label_propagation()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Detect communities by asynchronous label propagation. title: >- [Graph.cmty_label_propagation()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Detect communities by asynchronous label propagation. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Detect communities by asynchronous label propagation. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L40516-L40658){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.cmty_label_propagation( seed=None, max_iter=100, attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Label propagation communities](../assets/graphs/cmty-label-propagation.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Two dense clusters, a triangle A, B, C and a four-node cluster D, E, F, G, joined by the single edge C to D. Starting from one label per node, each node repeatedly adopts its neighbors' most common label; the labels settle on the two clusters, drawn in the accent color and teal. The card lists community 0 as A, B, C and community 1 as D, E, F, G." width="100%"} Every node starts with a label of its own. Nodes are then visited in random order, and each adopts the label carried by the most edges (or the most edge weight, on a weighted graph) among its neighbors, breaking ties at random. Labels spread through densely connected regions and stall at sparse boundaries; when a full pass changes nothing, each remaining label is a community (Raghavan, Albert & Kumara, 2007). Label propagation needs no parameters and runs in near-linear time, so it scales to very large graphs. It does not optimize any objective, and different seeds can give different partitions, so it is best for a fast first look; use `cmty_leiden()` when partition quality matters. Edge direction is ignored. This is the unsupervised community detection method that NetworkX calls `asyn_lpa_communities()`. It is different from `label_propagation()`, which spreads a few *known* labels to classify the remaining nodes. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Random seed for the visiting order and tie-breaking. Set it for reproducible results. [max_iter]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[100]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum number of passes over the nodes. Label propagation almost always settles much sooner; the cap guards against rare oscillations. Default is `100`. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute to store community labels in. If `None` (default), uses `"cmty_label_propagation"`. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns a dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores the community labels as a node attribute and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, int], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: a dictionary mapping node IDs to community labels (`0`, `1`, ..., numbered in order of the lowest node ID in each). If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): returns self. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~cmty_fast_label_propagation`) : Label propagation that revisits only changed nodes. [](`~cmty_semisync_label_propagation`) : Label propagation with the same result on every run. [](`~harmonic_function`) : Spread a few known labels to the other nodes. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Two triangles joined by a single edge each settle on one label: ::: {#eac4fbb6 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph.from_edges([ ("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E"), ("E", "F"), ("F", "D"), ]) ( graph.cmty_label_propagation(seed=1) .get_node_df() .select("label", "cmty_label_propagation") ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ### One network, many answers `dolphins()` is a social network of 62 bottlenose dolphins in Doubtful Sound, New Zealand, linked when they were seen together often. The visiting order and the tie-breaking are random, so each seed can settle on different communities: ::: {#c1728ceb .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import polars as pl dolphins = ec.dolphins().layout_kamada_kawai() rows = [] for seed in range(1, 9): found = dolphins.cmty_label_propagation(seed=seed, return_dict=True) rows.append({ "seed": seed, "communities": len(set(found.values())), "modularity": dolphins.modularity(found), }) pl.DataFrame(rows) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

Running several seeds and keeping the best, or using `cmty_leiden()`, gives a steadier answer: ::: {layout-ncol="2"} ::: {#f7022852 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} dolphins.cmty_label_propagation(seed=1, attr_name="seed_1") dolphins.plot( layout="pos", color_by="seed_1", edge_color_by="seed_1", show_labels=False, width=320, height=360, legend=False, ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
